verses.1: So, after traveling for three days from Caesarea, he arrived in Jerusalem.
verses.2: The high priests and the first among the Jews also appeared before him according to Paul’s teachings. They called upon him.
verses.3: We ask that he be sent to Jerusalem in his own person, so that he can be delivered along with his belongings during the journey.
verses.4: So, Phestos decided to stay with Paul in Caesarea, while he himself was about to be sent away.
verses.5: Those among you, they say, are capable of understanding what is wrong with that man. They accuse him of having something wrong with him.
verses.6: After spending less than eight or ten days among them, he went to Caesarea. In the evening, he ordered Paul to go ahead.
verses.7: And as a result of his actions, the Jews from Jerusalem tried to get rid of him. They tried to find many and heavy reasons to prove that he was not worthy of being released.
verses.8: Paul argued that they had not done anything wrong either against the laws of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against the Emperor.
verses.9: Then Phestos, wanting to give a response to the Jews, said to Paul, “Do you want to go to Jerusalem so that you can be judged there regarding these matters?”
verses.10: Pavlos said, “At this moment, I am in a position where I must be judged by those who have the authority to do so. I have not done anything wrong to the Jews, as you also know very well.”
verses.11: If I indeed do something wrong or deserve to die, then I won’t refuse to die. But if there’s nothing for which they can accuse me, then no one can give me any pleasure. I call them fools.
verses.12: Then, after consulting with the others, Phastesus spoke his opinion. Kaisara was called upon to give his opinion as well.
verses.13: On the days when Agrippa was alive, the king and Bernice took him to Caesarea, in order to defend Pheston.
verses.14: After enduring there for many days, Phastus addressed the king, saying, “What kind of man is this who has been bound by Phylkos’ chains?”
verses.15: Regarding this matter, the high priests and the elders of the Jews appeared before me in Jerusalem, demanding that I impose judgment upon him.
verses.16: To whom I replied that it is not customary for Romans to give someone a gift before the accused has been tried in person and can receive the punishment due to his crimes.
verses.17: So, after they had arrived there, I didn’t make any delays in proceeding with the plan. I ordered them to start moving forward.
verses.18: Regarding this, the judges offered no reason for me to be considered a wicked person.
verses.19: There were also certain questions regarding his own blindness, as well as regarding Jesus after he died. Paul believed that Jesus was still alive.
verses.20: I, however, was unable to fulfill this request. They said that if I wanted to go to Jerusalem, I should wait there and then be judged regarding these matters.
verses.21: When Paul was called to be examined by the bishop, I ordered that he be kept in custody until I could send him back to Caesar.
verses.22: Agrippa, on the other hand, spoke to Pheston. I also tried to listen to what that man said. On April, he said, he would listen to him.
verses.23: So, after Agrippa and Bernice arrived, after much hesitation, they went into the auditorium together with the hundreds of commanders and men who were always ready to serve in the city. Then, Paul was called forward.
verses.24: And Phestus said: “Agrippa, king, and all the men who were with us, consider this as a sign that all those Jews who were in Jerusalem and elsewhere have been defeated by me. They no longer deserve to live.”
verses.25: I, however, did not find anything worthy of his death. Therefore, when I called upon the Saint to take care of him, I decided to send him there.
verses.26: I don’t know what to write to the king without being sure of the details. Therefore, we’ve brought him before you, most especially to you, King Agrippa. So, what should I write after this investigation has taken place?
verses.27: For it seems to me that when one gives a gift, one should not take into account the reasons why it was given.
